description: Roadmap placeholder for the canonical worked example in docs/design-quality-standard.md's functional/mechanical track: a chip bag clip planned with flex/tension, material, and iteration considerations from the start - not just 'the minimum geometry that technically clips.' No CAD, mesh, or render exists for this concept.
considerations: material choice (PETG vs TPU vs PLA tradeoffs)
prototype_status: Functional objects under tension or repeated stress must be treated as prototypes until physically tested by a human - this repo never guarantees strength, food safety, or durability.

design_intent.use_case: reseal an opened chip bag and keep it airtight-ish on a shelf

visual_goals.silhouette: recognizable as a clip at a glance, not just a bent rectangle
visual_goals.proportions: grip area sized for adult fingers; jaw width matches common chip bag thickness
visual_goals.surface_detail: smooth, rounded edges - no sharp corners at the grip or hinge
visual_goals.color_material_intent: single material, color TBD - human decision before prototyping

functional_goals.primary_function: clamp a folded chip bag opening closed with enough force to stay sealed
functional_goals.tension_or_flex_notes: hinge area flexes on every use - fillet radii and wall thickness must be planned for repeated flex from the start, not discovered by breaking prototypes; see docs/design-quality-standard.md's functional/mechanical track

iteration_plan.prototype_strategy: print a small flex test strip in each candidate material before committing to the full clip
test_points: grip force check on an actual bag
iteration_plan.acceptance_notes: not print_ready or human_approved until physically tested - see prototype_status above

notes: This file uses `concept_brief.json`, not `brief.json`, so `factory` commands do not treat this directory as a real, in-progress project.
No STL, render, or other generated mesh asset exists for this concept.
This concept is not human_approved and not print_ready, and is not expected to pass factory review-gate.
This concept is not print_ready and not human_approved even after a future prototype pass - physical testing by a human is required first, every time.
design_intent is planning-only (see docs/design-intent-brief.md, Phase 24) - it is not read or validated by any factory command and never sets human_approved or print_ready.
